questions.prompt: What is the "good" threshold for Largest Contentful Paint (LCP)?
questions.explanation: LCP is good at ≤ 2.5 s, needs improvement up to 4.0 s, and poor above 4.0 s — measured at the 75th percentile of real visits.

questions.prompt: INP became a Core Web Vital in March 2024, replacing the older metric ____ (three-letter abbreviation).
questions.explanation: Interaction to Next Paint (INP) replaced First Input Delay (FID) on March 12, 2024. FID only measured the delay of the first interaction; INP is stricter.

questions.prompt: Which of these are the three Core Web Vitals? Select all that apply.
questions.explanation: The Core Web Vitals are LCP, INP, and CLS. FCP and TTFB are useful related metrics but are not Core Web Vitals.

questions.prompt: Match each Core Web Vital to its "good" threshold.
questions.explanation: Good bars: LCP ≤ 2.5 s (loading), INP ≤ 200 ms (responsiveness), CLS ≤ 0.1 (visual stability), all at the 75th percentile.

questions.prompt: An interaction's latency (measured by INP) is made of three parts. Order them as they happen.
questions.explanation: INP = input delay + processing time + presentation delay: the wait before handlers run, the handler work, then painting the visual response.

questions.prompt: What are the units of Cumulative Layout Shift (CLS)?

options.text: It is a unitless score (impact fraction × distance fraction)

questions.explanation: CLS is unitless — each shift scores impact fraction × distance fraction, and CLS sums the shifts in the worst session window. Good is ≤ 0.1.
